notes: On 1h, price crossing up EMA 20 gave 10,797 entries in 2,757 separate moves. Twenty candles later these entries were 0.01% behind random entries, inside the luck band. On 4h it fires about a quarter as often and ends 0.04% ahead, which is also the same as random. McGinley Dynamic 20 crosses landed in the same place on both timeframes.

On 4h, entries while price was above SMA 200 beat random by 0.65% after 20 candles, across 171 separate moves. The pooled result holds without its strongest stretch and at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles. Pair by pair, each result rests on one stretch, such as SOL's between Jan 1, 2021 and May 21, 2021. On 1h the same filter did the same as random.

Split by regime, price above SMA 200 on 4h beat random in uptrends by 0.45%, and that result rests on the stretch between Jul 29, 2021 and Sep 27, 2021. In downtrends it did the same as random. The pooled number is an uptrend result, not one that covers both regimes.

On 1h, shorting as SMA 50 crossed down SMA 200 beat random by 0.42% after 20 candles. It holds without its strongest signal and at 50 and 100 candles, but not at 10. SOL carries it at 0.87%, and on BTC and ETH it did the same as random. In uptrends it did the same as random. In downtrends the gain rests on two signals on Apr 6, 2025.

The golden cross did the same as random on 1h and 4h, and EMA 50 crossing up EMA 200 did too. On daily, price crossing up a rising SMA 20 beat random by 7% after 20 days, but only at that horizon. In uptrends the same setting beat random by 10% and held without its strongest stretch at 10 and 20 candles, though not at 50 or 100. In downtrends there were too few moves to judge.

For a long DCA bot, a cross of price over EMA 20 or a golden cross adds no timing on these pairs, so the DCA orders and take profit do the work. Price above SMA 200 on 4h is the setting worth testing as a filter beside your own entry condition. It breaks when the trend turns: below the daily 200 SMA, the filter did the same as random. A rising daily SMA 20 is worth a backtest as a filter, not as the trigger.
